To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression and detection of ORF2-encoded proteins are highly dependent on the presence of the ORF2 tag and that ORF2 protein expression is stochastic in cells expressing L1.

1) the expression and detection of L1-encoded proteins is highly variable, 2) the expression and purification of ORF2-tagged ORF1p from native L1 constructs is not possible, 3) the expression of ORF1- and ORF2-tag fusion proteins from ORFeus-HS is variable, and 4) the ORFeus-HSpORF2p protein is expressed at low levels in a stochastic fashion.
the ORF1p/2p ratio in the native L1RP is 1:1, while in the ORFeus-HS it is 1:2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression, detection and purification of L1 ORF-encoded protein products and their role in L1-mediated retrotransposition.
the development of tools and methods for detection of ORF2 protein, which is a critical step towards a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms of L1 retrotransposition.
the expression and detection of L1-encoded proteins and how this affects the retrotransposition of synthetic L1s.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of ORF1p and the expression of ORFe2p are both controlled at the level translation.
ORF2p expression is not only difficult to detect but is also stochastic.
the ORFeus-HS system is a more reliable and reproducible system for the detection and purification of the L1 ORF2 protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully identified several epitope tags that allow robust detection of ORF1p and, in some cases, ORF2 protein expression in vitro and in mammalian cells.
the ORF1p and the ORF2p are differentially translated from the bicistronic L1 mRNA.
the expression of ORF1p and 2p are controlled at the translational level, and that the tag sequences used in this work do not affect ORF protein expression or retrotransposition competency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ORF2p can be detected in L1-express ing cells and that it is expressed at levels that are sufficient for its incorporation into L1RNPs.
ORF2p can be readily detected and purified from L1-expressin cell lines, and that ORF2 expression is not necessarily tightly controlled by the host-cell translation machinery.
L1 ORF2p expression is not a rare event, and that ORF1p and 2p can be detected in L1-express ing cells using epitope-tagged ORF proteins.
